channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan's OSON Holding Launches OSON X Platform at Dubai Fintech Summit
item.description: Kazakhstan's fintech group OSON Holding has introduced its OSON X application at the Dubai Fintech Summit. The service facilitates money transfers between the UAE and Central Asian countries like Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, and Tajikistan. OSON X is entering closed testing for institutional partners and focus groups.

item.title: Batken Authorities Address Resident Concerns Raised During Presidential Meeting
item.description: In Кызыл-Кыя, four out of six issues raised by residents during a meeting with President Sadyr Жапаров have been resolved. A working group, led by the regional governor, addressed concerns regarding water supply, schools, a factory's operations, and legal matters. Further investigation is underway for the remaining two issues.

item.title: Complex Brain Surgery Performed on Child with Pathology in Almaty
item.description: Neurosurgeons at Almaty's Children's Clinical Hospital No. 2, in collaboration with German colleagues, performed a complex surgery on an eight-year-old child. The team successfully removed a rare brain hamartoma, a congenital pathology causing neurological issues. The child had experienced seizures, developmental delays, and headaches.

item.title: Kazakh MP questions scientific basis of sanatorium mud and water therapies
item.description: A Member of Parliament in Kazakhstan has called for scientific validation of the therapeutic properties of mud, mineral, and thermal waters used in local sanatoriums. MP Ekaterina Smolyakova argued that claims of healing effects need scientific proof, urging for legislative mechanisms to study and classify these natural resources for medical tourism.

item.title: Bishkek revokes developer's license for advertising housing project before foundation completion
item.description: Bishkek has suspended construction and revoked the license of developer 'SK Nobel' for advertising a residential complex before completing the 'zero cycle' of construction. The Ministry of Construction stated that advertising and sales are prohibited until the foundation and underground works are finished. The violation was discovered by the State Architectural and Construction Control Department.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Sadyr Japarov Amends Rules for Citizen Complaints
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov has signed a law altering the procedures for electronic citizen complaints to government bodies. The new rules mandate electronic signatures for responses and require state bodies to notify citizens of complaint outcomes via the same channel they were submitted.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Sambo Wrestlers Win 7 Medals at World Championship
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's national sambo team secured one gold, one silver, and five bronze medals at the World Sambo Championship held in Tashkent, Uzbekistan. The State Agency for Physical Culture and Sports reported the team's success in the competition, which took place from November 6-8.

item.title: Former Education Minister Gani Beisembayev awarded 500,000 tenge in defamation case
item.description: A court in Almaty has partially granted a lawsuit filed by former Education Minister Gani Beisembayev against journalist Gulnara Bazhenova. Beisembayev sued over social media posts alleging his familial ties influenced career advancements. The court ruled the publications were false and damaging to his honor and reputation, awarding him 500,000 tenge in moral damages.

item.title: Kazakhstan Foreign Ministry Confirms Advanced EU Visa Facilitation Talks
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs has confirmed that negotiations regarding the simplification of the Schengen visa regime are in an advanced stage. A spokesperson expressed gratitude to European partners for their understanding and optimism for a positive outcome within a reasonable timeframe.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan: Parliamentary Audit Reveals Delays in Uzgen District Infrastructure Projects
item.description: A parliamentary committee inspection in Kyrgyzstan's Uzgen district has uncovered significant delays in the construction of a new medical center, road reconstruction, and school projects. The medical center, budgeted at 1.35 billion soms, faces challenges with subcontractor work and funding, impacting its completion timeline.

item.title: Iran Defends Peace Talks Proposal After US Rejects Conditions
item.description: Iran defended its proposal for peace talks, suggesting they could restart in two days, after US Secretary of State Marco Rubio called some conditions "outrageous." Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman questioned the unreasonableness of demanding the lifting of US sanctions and naval blockades before negotiations and an end to the war on all fronts.

item.title: Ukraine Attacks Major Russian Oil Refinery in Leningrad Region with Drones
item.description: Ukraine launched a drone attack on Russia's Leningrad region overnight, targeting the Kirishi Nefteorgsintez oil refinery, Russia's second-largest. The refinery, which produces gasoline, diesel, and aviation fuel, has been attacked previously. Regional authorities reported a civilian fatality in Vsevolozhsk due to falling drone debris.

item.title: Western Banks Eye Kazakhstan Market, Facing Entry Barriers
item.description: Western banks are considering expanding their presence in Kazakhstan, potentially focusing on the corporate segment rather than retail. Despite Kazakhstan's developed financial infrastructure and high banking profitability, challenges remain for foreign players entering the market.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans 18% Annual Interest Loans for Domestic Appliance Purchases
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to launch a consumer credit program offering 18% annual interest loans for purchasing locally manufactured home appliances. This initiative aims to make appliances more accessible to the public and boost sales for domestic producers.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Reports Over 10,000 Cases of ARVI and Flu, Primarily Among Children
item.description: From November 2 to November 11, Kyrgyzstan recorded 10,900 cases of acute respiratory viral infections (ARVI) and influenza. The Ministry of Health reported a 4.4% increase compared to the previous week and a 1.6-fold rise compared to the same period in 2025. Children under 14 constitute 71.1% of cases.

item.title: Uzbekistan Mandates Local Electronics Use in State-Supported Investment Projects
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to boost domestic demand for local electronics by requiring their use in large investment projects receiving state benefits. Projects valued over $10 million, utilizing tax breaks or subsidized resources, must now include a minimum percentage of local products, aligning with existing energy sector requirements.

item.title: Tajikistan Sets 18-Year Minimum Age for Labor Migrants
item.description: Tajikistan has legally established a minimum age of 18 for its citizens seeking employment abroad. The new law, signed by President Emomali Rahmon, replaces the 1999 migration law. It also applies to foreign nationals seeking work in Tajikistan, ensuring protection of labor migrants' rights through international and bilateral agreements.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Sadyr Japarov reviews development plans for Moscow district
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov reviewed the socio-economic development results for the Moscow district for 2021-2026. He was informed about ongoing and future investment projects, including the construction of the Ak-Suu regulating basin, which will provide irrigation for 2,048 hectares of agricultural land.

item.title: Uzbekistan introduces corruption resistance checks for civil servants
item.description: Uzbekistan has approved a procedure for testing civil servants for corruption resistance. Officials will be assessed on a 600-point system, with scores impacting their eligibility for positions with high corruption risks. The checks will be conducted every three years and upon hiring.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Ministry of Agriculture to meet with processors on business support
item.description: The Kyrgyz Ministry of Agriculture has invited entrepreneurs and representatives of the processing industry to a meeting on November 10. Participants will discuss industry challenges and business proposals as part of the '1000 Days' reform. Key topics include domestic production development and reducing business barriers.

item.title: Uzbekistan to publish three-year public procurement plans in advance from 2027
item.description: Uzbekistan will announce its three-year public procurement plans in advance starting January 1, 2027. This new regulation will allow businesses to better estimate product demand, expand production, and attract investors. The announcement aims to improve transparency and planning in public procurement.

item.title: Third Uzbek-Russian Media Forum to be Held in Tashkent
item.description: The third Uzbek-Russian Media Forum will take place in Tashkent, focusing on cooperation between the two countries, the role of media in promoting traditional values, and current media landscape challenges. Representatives from government bodies, leading media, and NGOs will attend the event organized by UzA and TASS.

item.title: Developer of Asman City Granted Five-Year Tax Exemptions
item.description: The Kyrgyz government has granted 'RedStone Group,' the developer of the eco-friendly Asman City project, tax benefits for five years. This includes zero VAT and sales tax rates on goods, works, and services for the project, as well as for imported goods. 'RedStone Group' is the sole company on the approved list.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's First Deputy Prime Minister Addresses Economic Concerns
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's First Deputy Prime Minister Daniyar Amangeldiev discussed the nation's economy, state debts, and support for businesses. He acknowledged personal miscalculations in the distribution of state support. Amangeldiev also addressed rising prices for essential goods and the impact on families, explaining that economic growth is visible through job creation and infrastructure development.

item.title: Kazakhstan Considers Three-Year Moratorium on Inspections for Small Businesses
item.description: Kazakhstan is considering a three-year moratorium on inspections for micro and small businesses, effective January 1, 2027. The specific conditions and exemptions are still under discussion. Experts advise entrepreneurs to consider past moratorium experiences, which saw a significant reduction in inspections, though other factors like pandemic restrictions also played a role.

item.title: Aktau Residents Left Without Heat at Start of Heating Season
item.description: Residents in several districts of Aktau are without heating at the beginning of the official heating season. City authorities state that the power plant is operating normally, attributing the cold apartments to the lack of managing organizations within the buildings. Residents are advised to address complaints directly to the housing inspection.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Electrotechnical Sector Achieves 50 Trillion Sum Production Value
item.description: Uzbekistan's electrotechnical industry produced 50 trillion sums in 2026, a significant increase from 1.7 trillion sums in 2016. Over the past decade, $2 billion was invested, 413 new production facilities were launched, and over 100 new products were introduced. Exports grew 14-fold, reaching $1.6 billion this year.

item.title: Nearly 100 Citizens Receive Free Legal Aid in Kyrgyzstan's Chuy Region
item.description: During meetings with residents of Kyrgyzstan's Chuy region, nearly 100 citizens received free legal consultations and submitted written applications. Ministry of Justice officials organized mobile reception points in several cities and districts. Applications received are under personal supervision of the ministry's leadership.

item.title: New Director Appointed at Almaty RFMSh Following Student Food Poisoning Incident
item.description: Almaz Kungozhin has been appointed the new director of the Almaty branch of the Republican Physics and Mathematics School (RFMSh). This follows a mass food poisoning incident where 58 students were hospitalized with acute intestinal infections in October 2026 due to violations in the school's food block.

item.title: Monthly Income Required for a 30 Million Tenge Mortgage in Kazakhstan
item.description: To purchase an apartment worth 30 million tenge with a mortgage in Kazakhstan, individuals need an official monthly income of at least 722,000 tenge. This calculation assumes a 20% down payment and considers the debt-to-income ratio, which banks limit to 50% of monthly earnings. Additional income sources or a co-borrower may be required.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Citizens to Travel to Seychelles Visa-Free for Up to 30 Days
item.description: Kyrgyz citizens will be able to travel to Seychelles without a visa for stays of up to 30 days per trip, following the ratification of an agreement signed on May 11, 2026. The total duration of stay within a calendar year must not exceed 90 days. The law ratifying the agreement will take effect 10 days after its official publication.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Compensate Up to $50,000 for International Financing Attraction
item.description: Uzbekistan will reimburse up to $50,000 in expenses for electrical engineering enterprises attracting international financing. The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) is also prepared to provide $2-3 billion to industrial enterprises. This initiative aims to help local producers access international financial markets and expand production.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Tax Service Urges Businesses to Update Product Catalogs by March 2027
item.description: The State Tax Service of Kyrgyzstan has called on entrepreneurs to align their product, work, and service names with a new electronic catalog by March 1, 2027. This catalog is a key component of the updated electronic invoice system, ESF 2.0. Businesses must submit requests for any missing items through their online tax accounts.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Host World Championships in Five Sports in 2027
item.description: Kazakhstan will host world championships in boxing, judo, taekwondo, table tennis, and esports in 2027, President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev announced. He emphasized sports' role in international reputation and public diplomacy, stating Kazakhstan aims to strengthen its position as a sports power by organizing high-level international competitions. A junior short-track speed skating championship is also planned.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Implement International Vocational Education System in 45 Technical Schools
item.description: Uzbekistan is expanding its international professional qualifications program to 45 state technical schools, expecting to enroll 3,500 more students in the 2026/2027 academic year. This initiative, a collaboration between Uzbekistan's Professional Education Agency and Pearson, aims to equip students with skills in engineering, IT, construction, tourism, hospitality, healthcare, and social care.

item.title: Uzbekistan Investigates Food Poisoning of Kazakh Children at Football Tournament
item.description: Uzbekistan is investigating a food poisoning incident that affected Kazakh children during a football tournament in Tashkent. The Kazakh Foreign Ministry stated that all affected children have returned home and received treatment with Uzbekistan's support. Kazakhstan is not participating in the investigation, as it is being conducted by Uzbek law enforcement.

item.title: Uzbekistan Introduces New Benefits for Robotics and High-Tech Industries
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev announced new benefits for Uzbekistan's robotics and high-tech sectors. Enterprises in the new "Center of Future Technologies" in Nurafshon will receive IT park resident benefits. Import duties on raw materials for robotics and electronics will be waived, and income from related scientific research will be tax-exempt.

item.title: UN Human Rights Council Urged to End Persecution of Journalists and Opposition in Tajikistan
item.description: At the UN Human Rights Council, Western nations called on Tajikistan to cease persecution of journalists, activists, and political opponents, release arbitrarily detained individuals, and stop pursuing Tajiks abroad. Tajikistan's Justice Minister reported on human rights progress, including a new strategy and legal reforms, while downplaying concerns about media freedom.

item.title: Court hears case of alleged theft of granite tiles during Almaty river reconstruction
item.description: A court in Almaty heard testimony regarding the alleged theft of granite tiles during the reconstruction of the Bolshaya Almatinka river. The prosecution claims Sanjar Bokayev and his videographer organized the theft and created a video blaming city officials. A representative from the ecology department testified to reputational damage.

item.title: President Meets Athletes Who Won Medals at Asian Games and Para Games
item.description: The President met with athletes who received medals at the Asian Games and Para Games. This meeting highlights the recognition and celebration of Kazakhstan's sporting achievements on the international stage. The event underscores the importance placed on sports and athlete success by the nation's leadership.
